headline: Surgeons Save Monkey's Foot—Then She Becomes a Mother
meta_description: A critically endangered roloway monkey at Chester Zoo kept her foot after pioneering surgery, then gave birth to a daughter—a rare win for a species with fewer…
summary_short: Masaya, a 15-year-old roloway monkey, underwent complex foot surgery at Chester Zoo. Months later, she delivered her daughter Lagertha—a significant birth for one of Ear…
body:
Masaya, a 15-year-old roloway monkey at Chester Zoo, has given birth to a healthy daughter named Lagertha just months after undergoing pioneering surgery that saved her foot from amputation. The critically endangered primate developed a golf-ball-sized mass on her foot and faced the prospect of losing the limb entirely until veterinarians from Chester Zoo partnered with surgeons from the University of Liverpool's Small Animal Teaching Hospital to attempt an innovative removal. The medical team found no previous record of this procedure being performed on a roloway monkey, yet the operation succeeded, allowing Masaya to retain all but one toe. The timing of her recovery proved crucial: had amputation been necessary, staff worried she might struggle to hold and care for her offspring.

Masaya's birth of Lagertha—her third daughter—carries profound significance for a species facing extinction. Fewer than 2,000 roloway monkeys remain in the wild across Ghana and the Ivory Coast, threatened by habitat destruction and poaching. Chester Zoo is one of only two places in the United Kingdom where the species can be found, and Masaya is part of a coordinated European breeding program designed to prevent the species' disappearance. Zoe Edwards, the primate keeper, noted that there are only a few breeding females in European zoos, making each successful birth invaluable.

Masaya's foot troubles had plagued her since arriving at Chester Zoo in 2023, with veterinarians unable to determine the underlying cause despite X-rays, ultrasounds, and biopsies. Staff eventually suspected a persistent abscess, possibly stemming from an old thorn injury. By 2025, the swelling worsened enough to warrant the trip to Liverpool for detailed imaging and surgery. Today, Masaya has recovered well, and young Lagertha—named after a Viking queen—is thriving alongside her mother and four other monkeys in the habitat.
quick_facts: Masaya kept all but one toe after pioneering foot surgery
Fewer than 2,000 roloway monkeys remain in the wild
Lagertha is Masaya's third daughter and third monkey born at Chester Zoo
Surgery performed by University of Liverpool surgeons and zoo veterinarians
Species threatened by habitat loss across Ghana and Ivory Coast
